items.title: 14'' MacBook Pro, M5 Pro, 48GB of RAM, 1TB (2026)
items.description: Silent under load. All-day battery. 48GB of RAM runs agents, dev servers and the browser at once.

items.title: Dell S2722QC 27'' 4K USB-C
items.description: 4K text at 27 inches. A single USB-C cable carries video and charges the laptop. Clean desk.

items.title: BONTEC monitor arm
items.description: The monitor floats and the desk clears. Any brand holds 10 kg. Buy the cheap one.

items.title: Apple Magic Keyboard with Touch ID
items.description: Touch ID is the purchase: sudo, the password vault and the App Store on one fingerprint. The typing itself is fine.

items.title: Keychron M5 Wireless Ergonomic Mouse
items.description: Vertical enough to spare the wrist, normal enough to aim. Quiet clicks and 8K polling.

items.title: iPhone 17 Pro + Belkin MagSafe mount
items.description: The best webcam Apple sells is the phone. The Belkin clip snaps it to the lid, and Continuity Camera does the rest.

items.title: AirPods Pro 2
items.description: The noise cancellation erases an open office. Others sound better. None mic better.

items.title: Firmoo glasses
items.description: Blue-filter glasses are commodity optics. These are ten euros, made to prescription. Never pay boutique prices for a coating.

items.title: IKEA BEKANT (custom firmware)
items.description: Stock firmware moves the desk only during a button hold. I reflashed the PIC16LF1938: one press now travels to a saved height.

items.title: Interstuhl UPis1 100U
items.description: Hands down, this removes lower back pain. It is a stool with a rounded base, so you stabilize yourself all the time. Height is a non-issue with the desk above.

items.title: IKEA ALEFJÄLL, Grann beige
items.description: Real grain leather, adjustable everything, a ten year guarantee, an IKEA price. The back holds eight hours without complaint. Beige: a desk chair does not need to look like a cockpit.

items.title: DeltaHub Carpio 2.0
items.description: Gel pads press straight on the nerve. The Carpio lifts the wrist one centimeter and glides with the arm. A surgeon co-designed it.

items.title: Zed
items.description: Rust and GPU rendering: the window opens before the hand leaves the keyboard. The agent panel is native. Open source.

items.title: iTerm2
items.description: Split panes, instant replay, tmux integration. Fifteen years of releases and none broke anything. Boring, native, correct.

items.title: Fish shell
items.description: The terminal is nice, but have you ever played with shells? This is the real deal. Fish is out of this world.

items.title: Rosé Pine theme
items.description: All natural pine, faux fur and a bit of soho vibes. Their words. 220 ports, so every window wears the same palette.

items.title: Zed Mono (or Menlo)
items.description: Zed Mono ships with the editor, Menlo with the machine. Always favour the standards.

items.title: Safari (+ Chrome for DevTools)
items.description: Safari for living: battery and Keychain. Chrome for work: DevTools is DevTools. Two browsers, two jobs.

items.title: Claude Code
items.description: It reads the repo, runs the tests and writes the boring half. The terminal has a coworker now.

items.title: Codex CLI
items.description: Claude writes, so a rival reviews. Codex gets the diff cold and one instruction: attack. If both agree, the code ships.

items.title: Apple Notes
items.description: No Notion, no Obsidian, as easy as that. One keystroke, automatic sync, text. Never pay for a notes app.

items.title: dotfiles
items.description: All my cool configs. Steal anything you want. My aliases are legendary.

items.title: Apple everything
items.description: I degoogled completely: Mail, Calendar, Passwords, iCloud, Music. Apple charges money and treats me as the customer, not the product.

items.title: Raycast
items.description: My beloved. Launcher, clipboard history, window tiling, unit math, one hotkey. Anything with an API becomes a keystroke.

items.title: Affinity
items.description: Vector, pixel and layout in one window. Canva bought it and made it free. Pro tools, no monthly toll.

items.title: Klack
items.description: Every keypress gets a mechanical thock, in spatial audio. The Magic Keyboard sounds like switches now. Pocket change.

items.title: MonitorControl
items.description: The MacBook brightness keys drive the Dell over DDC. Free, open source, one menu bar icon. How does Apple not include this by default?

items.title: Ghostery + Hush
items.description: Ghostery strips the trackers. Hush strips the cookie banners in Safari. Both free. Never pay to un-break the web.

items.title: Yaak
items.description: Postman grew a login wall and a sync cloud. Yaak sends requests: REST, GraphQL, gRPC, plain files under git. Local-first, MIT, zero telemetry.

items.title: QuickTime Player
items.description: Screen recording ships with macOS: File, New Screen Recording, done. No watermark, no account, no extra app.

items.title: Qwant
items.description: The degoogle ends at the search box. European, no ad profile. The results are good enough to forget about.
